label: Second Triumvirate formed
detail: Octavian (named Caesar's heir in his will), Mark Antony and Lepidus take joint emergency powers.

label: Conspirators defeated at Philippi
detail: Antony and Octavian defeat Brutus and Cassius.

label: Battle of Actium
detail: Octavian's fleet defeats Antony and Cleopatra.

label: Egypt becomes a Roman province
detail: Octavian annexes Egypt after the deaths of Antony and Cleopatra.

label: Augustus becomes first emperor
detail: The Senate grants Octavian the title Augustus; start of the Principate.

label: Caesar officially deified
detail: The Senate recognises Caesar as a state god.

label: Successor kingdoms rule former Western provinces
detail: Germanic-led kingdoms such as the Ostrogoths, Visigoths and Franks hold power in former Western territories.

label: Frankish kingdom grows into a major Western power
detail: Under the Merovingian and later Carolingian dynasties.

label: Charlemagne crowned emperor
detail: The imperial title is revived in the West.

label: Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire continues
detail: The eastern half of the empire survives for nearly a thousand years.

label: Justinian's campaigns to reconquer the West
detail: Begins with the war against the Vandals in North Africa.

label: Fall of Constantinople
detail: The Byzantine state ends when Ottoman forces capture its capital.

label: Historians debate how abrupt the change was
detail: Some historians describe a gradual transformation of the Roman world rather than a sudden collapse.

label: Muslim community established at Medina
detail: The first Muslim community-state takes shape.

label: Islamic calendar counts years from the Hijra
detail: The calendar was introduced later; year 1 is the year of the Hijra.

label: Rapid expansion of Muslim-ruled territory
detail: Within about a century Muslim rule extended from Iberia to Central Asia.

label: Umayyad caliphate
detail: First hereditary caliphate, ruling from Damascus.

label: Abbasid caliphate replaces the Umayyads
detail: Dynastic change in the caliphate.

label: Baghdad founded
detail: Caliph al-Mansur founds the new Abbasid capital.

label: Umayyad emirate in Cordoba
detail: A branch of the Umayyads establishes rule in Iberia.

label: Mass mortality in Europe
detail: A large share of Europe's population died in the following years; estimates vary by region and source.

label: Labour shortages
detail: With fewer workers, labour became scarcer in many regions.

label: Statute of Labourers (England)
detail: An attempt to hold wages at pre-plague levels.

label: Peasants' Revolt in England
detail: Tensions over labour laws and taxation are often cited among its background causes; historians stress multiple causes.

label: Persecution of Jewish communities
detail: Plague rumours led to massacres of Jews in several European towns, for example Strasbourg in 1349.

label: Plague outbreaks recur
detail: Plague returned in waves for centuries.

label: End of the Byzantine Empire
detail: The last remnant of the Roman state in the East ends.

label: Constantinople becomes the Ottoman capital
detail: The city, later known as Istanbul, becomes the centre of Ottoman rule.

label: Ottoman power grows in southeast Europe and the eastern Mediterranean
detail: Ottoman expansion continued in the following decades.

label: Greek scholars move to Italy
detail: Some Byzantine scholars settled in Italy; historians debate how much this shaped the Renaissance, since contacts began earlier.

label: Search for alternative trade routes
detail: A traditional explanation for European maritime exploration; historians note Portuguese voyages began decades earlier.

label: Sustained European contact with the Americas
detail: Start of lasting contact between Europe and the Americas.

label: Columbian exchange of crops and animals
detail: Maize and potatoes spread to the Old World; horses and wheat were introduced to the Americas.

label: Epidemic disease among indigenous peoples
detail: Diseases introduced from Europe caused severe population decline; the scale is debated.

label: Spanish colonisation begins
detail: Spanish settlement starts in the Caribbean and spreads to the mainland.

label: Treaty of Tordesillas
detail: Spain and Portugal agree to divide newly encountered lands.

label: Fall of Tenochtitlan
detail: Spanish forces and indigenous allies conquer the Aztec capital.

label: Plantation economies and the transatlantic slave trade
detail: Colonial economies drove demand for forced labour. The voyages database records about 12.5 million people embarked between 1501 and 1866 (see the Data Analysis page).

label: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
detail: Adopted in August 1789 (see the Archive).

label: Monarchy abolished; First Republic proclaimed
detail: The French monarchy ends.

label: Louis XVI executed
detail: The king is put to death in January 1793.

label: Haitian Revolution
detail: Enslaved people in Saint-Domingue rise in 1791, in a colonial setting shaped by revolutionary France.

label: Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars
detail: A long series of wars involving France and most European powers.

label: Napoleon takes power
detail: Napoleon Bonaparte seizes power in a coup.

label: Congress of Vienna
detail: The powers redraw the European order after the Napoleonic Wars.

label: Battle of Waterloo
detail: Napoleon is defeated by Allied armies.

label: Collapse of empires
detail: The German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Ottoman empires ended between 1917 and 1922.

label: Russian Revolution
detail: Strain from the war contributed to the fall of the tsarist state.

label: Soviet Union formed
detail: The USSR is established.

label: Treaty of Versailles
detail: Peace settlement with Germany.

label: Debated link to the Second World War
detail: Historians disagree about how much the settlement contributed to later conflict.

label: League of Nations created
detail: International organisation founded after the war.

label: United Nations succeeds the League
detail: The UN Charter is signed in San Francisco.

label: India and Pakistan become independent states
detail: British India is divided.

label: East Pakistan becomes Bangladesh
detail: A later development within the state created in 1947.

label: Mass displacement
detail: Millions were displaced across the new border; estimates of the total vary widely.

label: Kashmir dispute
detail: The first India-Pakistan war began in 1947; the dispute continues.

label: Revolutions across the Eastern Bloc
detail: The fall of the Wall came amid a wider wave of change in Eastern Europe.

label: European Union enlargement of 2004
detail: Several former Eastern Bloc states joined the EU.

label: German reunification
detail: East and West Germany unite in October 1990.

label: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
detail: Part of a wider chain of events with multiple causes.

label: Rupert of the Palatinate elected
detail: Elected at Rhens on 21 August 1400 and crowned on 6 January 1401; Wenceslaus never accepted the deposition.
source: Wikipedia: Rupert, King of the Romans

label: Rupert dies; double election
detail: Rupert died on 18 May 1410. Sigismund was elected by three electors on 10 September and Jobst of Moravia by four on 1 October; Jobst died on 18 January 1411.

label: Wenceslaus keeps the Bohemian crown
detail: He stayed King of Bohemia until his death in 1419 and still regarded himself as rightful king of the Romans.

label: Sigismund takes Wenceslaus into custody
detail: Sigismund, with Bohemian noble support, imprisoned his half-brother; Wenceslaus later escaped.

label: Wenceslaus dies; Sigismund is heir
detail: Wenceslaus died on 16 August 1419 and Sigismund was his heir to the Bohemian crown.

label: Hussite Wars
detail: Religious and political conflict in Bohemia in which Hussites resisted Sigismund's claim to the crown.

label: Crusades against the Hussites
detail: The papacy proclaimed five crusades against Hussite Bohemia; Sigismund took part in the campaigns.

label: Battle of Lipany
detail: On 30 May 1434 moderate Hussites and Catholics defeat the radical Taborites, virtually ending the Hussite Wars.

label: Sigismund accepted as King of Bohemia
detail: The Compactata of July 1436 finally gave Sigismund rule over Bohemia.

label: Sigismund elected King of the Romans
detail: After Rupert's death and the death of Jobst, Sigismund became king of the Romans, while also King of Hungary.

label: Council of Constance
detail: Held under Sigismund's patronage, 1414-1418.

label: Western Schism ended
detail: The council ends the split in the papacy with the election of Pope Martin V.

label: Jan Hus executed
detail: The Bohemian reformer is burned at Constance; his death is a trigger for the Hussite movement's radicalisation.

label: Sigismund's responsibility for Hus's death
detail: Hus travelled under Sigismund's safe-conduct; historians debate how much responsibility Sigismund bears for his execution.

label: Imperial coronation in Rome
detail: The pope crowns Sigismund emperor.

label: Sigismund dies; Luxembourg male line ends
detail: Sigismund died in December 1437 and his daughter's husband, Albert of Habsburg, was his heir.

label: Albert II elected King of the Romans
detail: Elected at Frankfurt in March 1438.

label: Habsburgs hold the crown almost continuously
detail: The Habsburgs held the German kingship and imperial title almost without break until 1806; the main exception is Charles VII of Bavaria (1742-1745).

label: Was the deposition legitimate?
detail: The electors cited Wenceslaus's failure to end the papal schism and keep the peace; he and later writers disputed their right to depose a king.
